messages:
Lena Park: Customer follow-up: they want accurate per-route cost + fast link-to-trace. We need to pick between two implementation approaches for M2: pre-aggregate costs hourly (cheap reads) vs compute on read (more accurate but slower). Quick tradeoff and scope decision?

Kai Moore: Pre-agg pros: fast dashboard queries, predictable infra cost, easier to meet <2s SLA. Cons: lag (hourly) and more storage. Compute-on-read pros: near-real-time, better accuracy for short windows. Cons: higher CPU, tricky at scale.

Diego Alvarez: Backend reality: compute-on-read will need a cache layer and batching to avoid N^2. Cost-estimation is basically token attribution + model-run weights. We can do a hybrid: pre-agg for 1h windows + on-read for last-5m for hot routes. Effort: pre-agg ~4d infra + 2d backend; hybrid adds ~3d.

Maya Chen: UX ask: customer demo must show "now" view. If we ship only hourly pre-agg they'll complain. Hybrid solves demo expectation (show last-5m estimate) while keeping queries fast. For MVP keep filters minimal: time range quick presets (1h, 24h, 7d) and highlight last-5m estimate.

Arjun Singh: Ops concerns: compute-on-read spikes could impact serving. Hybrid is safer. Also need a safety throttle so dashboard queries can't trigger expensive recompute. Add an API quota + sampling cap.

Lena Park: Acceptance criteria proposal for M2 (hybrid): 1) Top-10 routes cost coverage >=85% for 24h; 2) "Now" estimate shown for last-5m with label "estimated"; 3) trace link resolves >=95% for sampled requests; 4) dashboard median query <1.8s under 95th perc load.

Kai Moore: Small UX tweak: show two columns: "24h cost" (pre-agg) and "live est (5m)". Live est should have tooltip: "computed from sampled requests".

Diego Alvarez: Implementation plan: Phase A (canary) = pre-agg pipeline + trace-link plumbing + live-est sampler for hot routes. Phase B = improve attribution accuracy, reduce sampler latency, add error-slice drilldown. I'll scope tickets.

Maya Chen: For demo I want synthetic traces and a seeded heavy route so live-est looks meaningful. Also mock the tooltip copy for legal review.

Arjun Singh: Runbook: if live-est compute causes >10% CPU bump on inference nodes, disable live-est and display pre-agg with notice. We'll expose a feature flag `obs_live_est` and an ops dashboard metric `live_est_cpu_delta`.

obs-bot: Canaries scheduled 2025-04-02 01:00-03:00 UTC. Join rollout channel #deploy-observability. :rocket:

Lena Park: Roadmap split (Sprint names): Sprint M2-canary (hybrid leaderboard, trace links, live-est for top-k), Sprint M3 (accuracy improvements, error-slice explorer, per-region breakdown). We cut per-user cost and long-term retention in M2.

Kai Moore: Agree with cuts. Also propose a small acceptance test: run dashboard query against synthetic dataset and assert live-est within +/-20% of ground truth for top route during demo.

Diego Alvarez: Noted. I'll add `cost_attribution_gap` metric and a nightly job to compute ground-truth diff on synthetic data in CI.

Maya Chen: UX acceptance checklist: layout mock, two-column label, estimated badge, trace open action, and demo dataset. I'll attach mocks to PRO-712.

Lena Park: Action items: Diego create PRO-712 (Hybrid leaderboard), Kai write tooltip copy, Maya upload mock + dataset, Arjun add runbook and ops metric. Customer demo booked for 4/16. Locking M2 scope unless major objections. :thumbsup:
